title: Finite integral coefficients admit a condensed two-term finite free resolution
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ with its valuation topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and let $a:O\to A$ be a continuous unital ring homomorphism. Regard $A$ as an $O$-module through $a$. Write $\underline O(S)=C(S,O)$ and $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ for the condensed ring sheaves on the site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and use module objects over $\underline O$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. There exist an integer $r\geq0$, an $O$-linear surjection $q:O^r\to A$ and an $O$-linear map $\phi:O^r\to O^r$ given by a matrix with entries in $O$ such that $q$ is continuous, $\phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $\ker q$ with its subspace topology, and
$$0\longrightarrow O^r\xrightarrow{\phi}O^r\xrightarrow q A\longrightarrow0$$
is exact as a sequence of $O$-modules. For every profinite set $S$, applying continuous functions gives an exact sequence of abelian groups
$$0\longrightarrow C(S,O^r)\xrightarrow{\phi\circ-}C(S,O^r)\xrightarrow{q\circ-}C(S,A)\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular $0\to\underline O^{\oplus r}\to\underline O^{\oplus r}\to\underline A\to0$ is an exact sequence of condensed $\underline O$-modules. The assertion includes $A=0$, for which $r=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions: exactness of the condensed finite free resolution of a finite O_E-algebra

proof.text: Enumerate all elements of A by Fin r, r=card A, and extend this family linearly from the coordinate basis to q:O^r→A. Basis vectors give surjectivity and LinearMap.continuous_on_pi gives continuity. This construction also covers the zero ring without a separate case.
Let K=ker q and c=card(A) in O. The additive group of A is killed by its cardinality, so c O^r lies in K. The positive integer c is nonzero since O is a subring of the characteristic-zero field E.

The integer-ring DVR theorem supplies the PID instance. Apply the Mathlib Smith normal form construction to K in O^r. Its embedding of the kernel-basis indices into the ambient-basis indices is surjective: an omitted ambient coordinate of c times its basis vector would be zero on K, giving c=0. Reindex the kernel basis along this bijection. The resulting equivalence eL:O^r≃K, followed by inclusion, defines the injective linear map φ with range K. Its standard matrix is LinearMap.toMatrix′ φ, and it is continuous by LinearMap.continuous_on_pi.

The recorded integer-ring profinite-tower theorem supplies compactness and Hausdorffness of O for precisely its recorded topology. Thus O^r is compact, and K has the Hausdorff subspace topology. The continuous bijection eL:O^r→K is closed, hence is a homeomorphism. This proves the required kernel homeomorphism without coordinate division.

Apply the already-proved continuousSections_finiteDiscrete_shortExact to φ and q, using the established algebraic exactness and kernel homeomorphism. Its component formulas identify its section maps with compLeftContinuous, and its condensed conclusion supplies the required specified arrows and short exactness.

Postcomposition by continuous O-linear maps is a morphism of the restricted regular continuous-section modules: verify naturality pointwise, and action compatibility on presheaf pure tensors using Sheaf.tensor_hom_ext. Identify continuousSectionsModule O O with the regular module since the scalar ring map is the identity. Coordinate projections and insertions give a bicone on r copies of that regular module. Their pairwise composites are Kronecker identities, and the sum of projection-insertion composites is the identity, sectionwise. The preadditive total-identity criterion and uniqueness of biproducts give the required finite-free identification. Combine this with the preceding clauses.
